Investigative Journalist. West Virginian.

EDUCATION
Columbia University Graduate School of Journalism May 2020
Master of Science | Toni Stabile Fellow in Investigative Reporting

Reported extensively on communities in the Bronx for The Bronx Ink. Produced multimedia stories of
national relevance with localized angles, including a story on the rise of young female politicians in the Bronx
and AOC’s response to blocking harassers on Twitter. Reported day-stories on deadline, including a story
about the participation of Bronx teens at the Youth Climate Strike. Served as a reporter and photo editor for a
month-long investigation into Bronx Housing Court. Was the top-ranked student in my reporting class and
awarded honors by my professors. Currently investigating charity fraud in connection with video game
streaming platforms and working under ProPublica’s Charles Ornstein.

Rochester Institute of Technology May 2017
Bachelor of Science in Journalism
Graduated one year early, summa cum laude, with a degree in journalism and minors in sociology and
anthropology, advertising and public relations, and marketing while competing as an NCAA student-athlete
(soccer). Recognized by the university as an Outstanding Undergraduate Scholar for maintaining a cumulative
GPA in the top | percent of the graduating class. Wrote extensively for RIT University News and freelanced as a
writer and photojournalist for local publications.

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE May. 2020 - Present
Mountain State Spotlight
Watchdog Reporter | Charleston, West Virginia

I shed light on — and help people understand — the barriers to health care that West Virginians face as part of a
small investigative team. I use a combination of data aggregation, open records requests and personal interviews
to uncover systemic failures. Then I help the public understand what those failures mean for them. When
possible, I approach my work with a solutions-oriented mindset. What is broken? How can officials fix it?

Fulbright Scholar Sept. 2018 - June 2019
Journalist and Researcher | Prishtina, Kosovo

Worked independently to produce a multimedia series on Kosovar women acting as catalysts for social
and political change. In June 2019, covered the Newborn Monument, the most recognized monument in
Kosovo, with the portraits of the 99 women interviewed for the project for a week-long interactive installation
that took place on the 20th anniversary of the end of the Kosovo War. The project was the subject of national
media attention. Volunteered as an editor for Kosovo 2.0, an online culture and politics magazine that publishes
in English, Serbian and Albanian. Among the pieces I edited was a Human Rights monograph (8 stories),
published on the United Nations Day for Human Rights.

Democrat and Chronicle / USA Today Network Aug. 2017 - June 2018

Suburban Reporter | Rochester, New York

Carried out investigations and reported on inequality linked to gender and place, local government, and
higher education. Helped lead months of in-depth coverage of a case of sexual harassment at the University of
Rochester, producing more than a dozen stories that resulted in the resignation of the university president. Two
of my sources were named among ‘The Silence Breakers,’ as TIME’s Person of the Year in 2017. Was awarded
the 2017 Distinguished Feature Writing Award for Excellence, a statewide recognition presented by New York
State Newspaper Publishers Association for a story exposing a regional trend in teen homicides connected to
dating violence. Previously served as an intern from June 2017 - August 2017.

Additional bylines: New York Times Opinion, USA Today, FourFourTwo Magazine, Kosovo 2.0.

SKILLS
Investigative: Experienced in Pacer, Orbis, LexisNexis, ACRIS, FOIA, and online verification techniques. IRE.
Multimedia: Extensive photo and audio reporting experience. Knowledge of Adobe Creative Suite.
Sports: NCAA and Conference All-Academic honors (soccer). United States Soccer Federation licensed coach.
